nugget: When I see the onboarding prompt on the new Time Logged page, it's the first thing I would look at.
I'm more likely than most people to actually read an onboarding prompt when something is new.
Most people would likely just click next through the onboarding prompt until it disappears and figure things out on their own as they go.
I assume the onboarding prompt includes all the important information I would need when questions come up eventually.
To see everyone's time for the last week on the Time Logged manager view, I would first select last week in the date picker.
To see everyone's time for the last week on the Time Logged manager view, I would select a team.
I found both the date selection and filtering by team on the Time Logged manager view very easy.
When adding time for a team, I wondered whether selecting a team lets me then exclude specific members, like removing Ryan from the product team, rather than adding time for everybody in the team.
I found adding two hours of time for a whole team at once very easy.
My only concern with the bulk add-time flow is understanding that if you select a team without further selecting specific team members, you're logging time for the entire team.
If I had no idea what was going on with a user's time log and needed to know what data was logged, I would go to the Time and Activity report rather than the individual time-log view.
To drill into one member's time log detail from the multi-member view, I would go to Actions and click View Time Logged.
Clicking on a user's name from View Time Logged switches the whole page to that specific user.
After clicking View Time Logged for a user, any action I take afterward, including the Add Time button, applies specifically to that user.
Showing which specific user I'm about to modify in the Add Time dialog is really helpful because it removes any doubt about who I'm editing.
I like that Hubstaff distinguishes between a time log entry and a work break in the Add Time dialog, because that distinction has concerned customers before.
For the Add Time dialog, it seems easy enough to select the date and the time range for a time entry.
In the Add Time dialog, I can see a summary of the total hours I'm adding.
In the Add Time dialog, I can assign a project and any associated to-dos if they exist.
In the Add Time dialog, the reason field is mandatory and I can add notes and mark the entry billable or not.
I think it would be a good idea to allow admins to modify either a single date or multiple dates at once in the Add Time dialog.

The timeline bar under the date in the Add Time dialog gives good visual confirmation of roughly where in the day the time is placed, which helps me catch mistakes like accidentally logging time in the morning instead of the afternoon because I didn't use 24-hour time.
I'm a visual person, so the timeline bar confirmation in the Add Time dialog is helpful for me.
I imagine the timeline bar in the Add Time dialog would be helpful for other people as well.
To view my own individual time entries from the multi-member view, my first thought would be to click on all members and then select myself.
As a CSM, I've definitely heard customers say that being able to enter work breaks would be helpful, especially when they've forgotten to note a break they took.
My biggest question mark about the redesign is the new page naming.
I think the naming 'Timesheets' versus 'Time Logged' / 'Time Tracked' is simple enough.
Having two sections on the same page, one called Time Tracked and one Time Logged, might be confusing.
Instead of labeling a section 'Time Tracked,' Hubstaff could label it 'Tracking,' since tracking is one of the main things Hubstaff is known for.
Whether the subsection under Tracking is called Time Logged or Time Tracked is immaterial to me; either would work.
Seeing both 'Time Tracked' and 'Time Log' as labels on the same page could make people ask 'wait, what's the difference?' and not realize that Time Tracked includes everything listed below it.
We use the verbiage 'tracking time' a lot when talking about Hubstaff.
Using the term 'Time Log' instead of 'tracking' might make it seem like something fundamental has changed about Hubstaff, when it hasn't.
I think 'daily Time Logged' is clear enough as a label, regardless of whether it says daily time tracked or daily time worked.
The only thing I would look for in Hubstaff's terminology is consistency in which word is used across the whole page.
Making a distinction between 'Time Worked' and 'Time Tracked' would confuse customers, because they would then ask us what the difference is.
I'm not sure Hubstaff should make a distinction between 'time worked' and 'time tracked' as separate concepts.
I would expect customers to understand 'Edit Time' and 'Add Time' the same way; either label would work.
I don't have an issue with the page being named 'Time Logged,' as long as it isn't easily confused with 'Time Tracked.'
As long as 'Time Logged' and 'Time Tracked' are clearly differentiated, with the tracked one referencing tracking specifically, either name is fine with me.
I've been wondering what the multi-selection checkbox on the Time Logged table does, since it's not currently working in the prototype.
I wondered whether the multi-selection checkboxes on the Time Logged table are meant to support making multiple edits at once.
Overall, the Time Logged experience seems pretty easy and straightforward to me.
I like the navigation in the new Time Logged experience; it's easy.
It was easy for me to find the things I was asked to do during the test.
Nothing was missing for me between the previous Timesheets experience and the new Time Logged experience.
I find the proposed pop-up text ('site narrowed down, updates instantly right where you are') concise and precise, and it matches what I just went through in the prototype.
I think customers will still be shocked by the redesign because most of our users aren't in the habit of checking a 'what's coming' section.
Hubstaff could add a banner or pop-up on the legacy page saying changes are coming soon, similar to what was done for the Time and Activity report during its legacy-to-new transition.
Having a 'changes are coming soon' notice would at least let Hubstaff say customers were told the change was going to happen.

Similar to timesheet approvals, where you can submit and approve for multiple people, being able to see more people at once and then exclude down to one or a specific team is always better than the reverse.
There will always be managers who want to see everybody's time at once just to glance and confirm everybody is tracking time while they're already on the timesheets page.
I had a lot of fun participating in this usability test.
